claim: A Python script sent through the Bash tool as a quoted heredoc does not receive a doubled backslash as written: '\\n' arrives as '\n', one backslash, which Python reads as a newline escape, so the script fails with an unterminated string or silently fails to match. A single backslash arrives unchanged.
evidence: Seen three times on 2026-11-19; reproduced 2026-11-26: a <<'EOF' heredoc holding s = "a\\nb" was written to the file as s = "a\nb" (Python: length 3). Which layer halves it is not confirmed against the tool's source.
use: Write the script to a file with the Write tool and run it, or build such strings with chr(10) / chr(92).

checked.how: Reproduced 2026-11-26 in this session: a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF') through the Bash tool holding s = "a\\nb" wrote s = "a\nb" to the file (cat shows one backslash), and Python printed len 3; a single backslash-n in the heredoc arrived unchanged (od -c: a \ n b). So the tool halves a doubled backslash; the newline is Python's reading of what is left.
